module_title: Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards - Technical Design, Controversies, and Constitution
introduction: Geared towards UPSC, State PCS, and CGL Tier-2, this advanced tier examines the constitutional validity of the awards, the physical metallurgy of the medallions, original nomenclature, and major historical controversies like the Subhas Chandra Bose incident.

core_concepts.title: Original Names of Padma Awards (1954)
core_concepts.description: Upon their inception in 1954, the Padma awards did not have their current names. They were collectively known as the 'Padma Vibhushan' and divided into three classes: 'Pahela Varg', 'Dusra Varg', and 'Tisra Varg'. They were renamed to Vibhushan, Bhushan, and Shri on January 8, 1955.

core_concepts.title: Constitutional Validity & Article 18(1)
core_concepts.description: Article 18(1) of the Indian Constitution abolishes titles. In the landmark 1995 case 'Balaji Raghavan vs. Union of India', the Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of these awards, ruling that they are 'honors', not 'titles'. Consequently, they cannot be used as a prefix or suffix to the recipient's name.

core_concepts.title: Physical Design of the Bharat Ratna
core_concepts.description: The medallion is designed in the shape of a Peepal leaf and is made of toned bronze (not gold). The obverse features a shining sun made of platinum with 'Bharat Ratna' written in Devanagari. The reverse features the State Emblem and 'Satyameva Jayate'. It is worn around the neck with a white ribbon.

core_concepts.title: The Subhas Chandra Bose Controversy (1992)
core_concepts.description: In 1992, the government announced the Bharat Ratna for Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose 'posthumously'. His family refused the award, arguing that there was no conclusive proof of his death. Following a Supreme Court petition, the award was officially cancelled, making it the only time a Bharat Ratna announcement was revoked.

important_entities.name: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
important_entities.significance: He initially declined the Bharat Ratna, arguing that those on the selection committee should not give the award to themselves. He was eventually awarded posthumously in 1992.

important_entities.name: D. C. Kizhakemuri
important_entities.significance: While posthumous awards existed for Bharat Ratna since 1955, D.C. Kizhakemuri became the first to receive the Padma Bhushan posthumously in 1999.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A massive trap! Students often assume the highest civilian honor comes with a huge cash prize. In reality, the Bharat Ratna carries a 'Zero Cash Prize'. It includes only a Sanad (certificate) signed by the President and the medallion.
Examiners will test you on the metal composition of the Bharat Ratna. The leaf structure is made of Toned Bronze, NOT Gold. Only the embossed sun is made of Platinum.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The year 1955 is critical because it introduced the current names (Vibhushan, Bhushan, Shri) and added the provision for posthumous Bharat Ratna awards.

exam_strategy_tips: For advanced exams like UPSC, intricately link the Balaji Raghavan (1995) Supreme Court ruling directly to Polity and Article 18. Understand that using these awards as titles can lead to forfeiture.
